quiz.authorAnyTopic: the course material I gave you
quiz.authorPrompt:
You are writing a quiz for a study app. Create a caq/v1 quiz JSON document I can import directly.

Topic: {{topic}}.
Exactly {{count}} questions, types limited to: {{types}}. Target difficulty {{difficulty}} of 5.

Hard requirements — the app validates every question and rejects invalid ones:
1. Output ONLY the JSON object, no commentary, no code fences.
2. Schema: {"": "caq/v1", "title": str, "questions": [...]}.
3. Per question: id (q1, q2, …), type (single|multi|truefalse|text|numeric|equation), stem_md (markdown; ALL math in LaTeX $...$), options_md (single/multi only, 3-5 options), answer (single: {"index": 0-based}, multi: {"indices": [...]}, truefalse: {"value": true|false}, text: {"value": str}, numeric: {"value": number, "tolerance": number}, equation: {"value": "LaTeX/sympy-parseable"}), explanation_md, concepts (1-3 atomic tags), skill (conceptual|procedural|applied|notation), bloom (remember|understand|apply|analyze|evaluate|create), difficulty (1-5), expected_time_sec (int).
4. Math must be correct — for equation answers, verify algebraically.
5. Distractors must be plausible but clearly wrong, each targeting a named misconception: add "misconceptions": {"<option index>": "snake_case_tag"}.
6. Questions must be self-contained (no references to outside material).

questionTypeInfo.composite: One multi-part problem; a later part answered correctly from your earlier answer earns follow-through credit.
questionTypeInfo.graph_read: Read a value off a generated curve or click the point asked for; the curve and the expected reading are computed by the app.
questionTypeInfo.code: Write Python code that runs in your browser against visible test cases — nothing is executed on a server.

exerciseKindInfo.multi_step: A guided multi-step problem: the tutor helps you through it with a hint ladder and independence score.
exerciseKindInfo.matching: Match each pair by dragging or picking.
exerciseKindInfo.ordering: Put the given items in the correct order.
exerciseKindInfo.categorize: Assign each item to the right category.
exerciseKindInfo.fill_blank: Complete the missing parts of a statement.
exerciseKindInfo.explain: Explain in your own words; graded by an AI rubric.
exerciseKindInfo.error_spot: Spot the error in a worked solution.
exerciseKindInfo.correct_solution: Fix the flawed line in a worked solution.
